source.title: Investigating Generalization in Neural Networks Under Optimally Evolved Training Perturbations

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; PDF extraction has some garbled symbols, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizers and reports that their relative generalization under deliberately corrupted training data differs from the usual account; this refines the scope of optimizer generalization claims.
record.gate_note: The study deliberately optimizes pixel perturbations in training data to widen the clean-test versus corrupted-training gap. Optimizer comparison results in Figure 3 are described qualitatively in the text; numerical values are figure-only. Other reported accuracy results concern perturbation-search methods and are not optimizer results.
record.test_reason: The study measures adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance in a new setting: training on optimized pixel corruptions and testing on clean images. Although the corruptions deliberately induce a generalization gap, the optimizer comparison measures their differing susceptibility; its objective does not explicitly enforce an adaptive-versus-SGD ranking.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: SGD is more resilient than adaptive optimizers to the optimized spurious training features, and its solution appears sharper along the plotted interpolation despite better generalization. The authors explicitly withhold a general conclusion that sharper minima are more robust.
record.recipe_differences: Training data are deliberately corrupted by optimized pixel perturbations; the study compares optimizers under this distribution shift rather than standard training on natural data. The evolutionary perturbation search is its own method.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice changes clean-test performance under optimally perturbed training data. The tested perturbation count and dataset vary across Figure 3 panels.

fits_no_version.finding: Along the interpolation between SGD and Adam weights, SGD has sharper geometry yet better clean-test performance under optimized training corruptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness along an optimizer-to-optimizer weight interpolation need not predict generalization under training-data corruption.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
record.problems: Optimizer performance values in Figure 3 are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text. Comparisons use deliberately corrupted training data and therefore do not establish optimizer rankings under standard natural-data training. The text does not state optimizer hyperparameter tuning details for this comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional optimizer rows are stated in text. Figure 4 compares interpolated SGD and ADAM weights and describes sharper SGD minima with better generalization, but it does not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness specified by V7, so no V7 row was extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Uncorrupted training, language benchmarks, a documented limited-tuning protocol, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD. Figure 3 does not quantify matched training performance.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Weight interpolation does not measure these properties.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the limits_scope verdict: testing only corrupted training data leaves ordinary training untested; it does not demonstrate a failure there. The optimizer ranking belongs under V4 rather than fits_no_version. Figure 4 is already declared in rows_left_out and does not test V7. Optimizer tuning details and the optimizer used during perturbation search are not specified in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and test-error trends.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Natural, uncorrupted training; language benchmarks; limited-tuning protocol; decoupled weight decay and switching from Adam to SGD.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and rankings against norm- and margin-based measures; optimizer-interpolated loss-surface comparison is related but does not measure the version's defined property.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: CNN (GrayNet)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD on optimally perturbed training data; evaluated on clean test data.
rows.uncertainty: one std dev. error shown; experiments performed 5 times
rows.note: Text says SGD consistently performs better than adaptive methods in all plotted cases; exact accuracy is not stated in text.
rows.check: SGD is the comparison arm: its higher clean-test accuracy supports the stated ranking. GrayNet's architecture is 24C3-P-48C3-P-256FC-10S; the record omits the second pooling layer. Exact accuracy is unavailable in the supplied text.

rows.operation_detail: Trained with ADAM on optimally perturbed training data; evaluated on clean test data.
rows.uncertainty: one std dev. error shown; experiments performed 5 times
rows.note: Authors state ADAM has prohibitively low testing accuracy across all cases.
rows.check: Adam's lower clean-test accuracy than SGD agrees with V4, rather than reversing it. Correct GrayNet to 24C3-P-48C3-P-256FC-10S. Exact accuracy is unavailable.

relationships.condition: GrayNet on MNIST with one perturbed pixel; ColorNet on CIFAR-10 with one and SVHN with two; training on optimized corruptions and evaluation on clean images.
relationships.reason: Section 4.3 and Figure 3 explicitly report SGD above Adam and RMSProp, with Adabound intermediate, across R1–R12; exact accuracies are unavailable.
relationships.display_finding: The reported clean-image accuracy advantage for SGD over Adam and RMSProp remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CNNs trained on optimally perturbed data and tested on clean MNIST, CIFAR10 and SVHN samples
reader_labels.reason: SGD consistently outperforms adaptive methods in the plotted settings; see R1, R5 and R9, compared with R2–R4, R6–R8 and R10–R12.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Training data deliberately corrupted with optimized pixel perturbations
reader_labels.reason: The optimizer comparison is under induced training distribution shift, so it does not establish the same ranking for natural, uncorrupted training; see R1–R12.
